thread:
alex: Quick sync — I sketched a simpler fairness + burst-credit model for Dedicated pools. Wanted feedback before turning into an RFC.

sara: please drop the sketch here, curious about how you handle simultaneous bursts across shards.

alex: TL;DR: each tenant gets a steady reservation + a small burst bucket that accrues over time. On admission we check: (steady_available >= req) || (burst_tokens >= req * burst_multiplier). Burst tokens decay slowly if unused.

alex: config example:```
pool: gpu-dedicated-prod
steady_reservation: 4
burst_bucket_capacity: 12
burst_accrual_rate_per_min: 0.5
burst_multiplier: 1.5
preempt_policy: gentle
```

tom: two quick concerns: 1) preemption churn — if we loosen admission with bursts we may force frequent evictions; 2) accounting complexity when requests span multiple slots.

alex: agree on churn. Proposal: add a soft-grace window (default 60s) where running jobs get a lease extension before eviction if new capacity is coming up. That reduces thrash.

lucy: observability note — we need per-tenant metrics: burst_tokens, accrual_rate, last_burst_use_ts, eviction_count. Also add a gauge for "expected_headroom" so SRE can see safety margin.

alex: good call. I sketched the telemetry tags: tenant_id, pool_shard, priority_class. Intended to back a regression alert: sudden drop in headroom or sustained burst burn > X for Y mins.

tom: what about fairness across shards? If tenant A uses bursts on shard 1 and tenant B on shard 2, you can end up with inequitable global service. Do we want cross-shard reconciliation?

alex: two options: per-shard isolation (simpler) or global token bank (harder but fairer). I'd default to per-shard for 1.0 to keep operator surface small, with a migration path to a global reconciler.

lucy: +1 to per-shard initially. If we go global later, we'll need periodic rebalance jobs and a consistent snapshot of tokens — that complicates rollout.

alex: rollout plan suggestion: feature-flag the burst bucket (off by default), enable for low-QPS tenants first, collect telemetry for 2 weeks, then enable progressive ramp.

alex: also thinking about admission API shape. Keep the runtime decision as a single boolean `admit` but include `admit_reason` and `used_burst_tokens` in the response for observability. So controllers can reconcile without re-running logic.

lucy: +1. That helps debugging and avoids mismatch between controller and runtime accounting.

tom: edge case: long-running requests that started using burst tokens then get preempted mid-run — how do we refund tokens?

alex: plan: tokens consumed at start of admission are tentatively reserved and only charged after a 30s confirmation tick; if preempted before confirmation, refund. Cheap UX but increases accounting delay. Thoughts?

lucy: sounds reasonable. We'll need to surface "tentative" state in metrics so alerts don't fire on short confirmation windows.

devops-bot: Deploy finished: feature/tenant-burst-token-telemetry -> staging (build #4821) :white_check_mark:

alex: thanks — i'll open an RFC draft with the config schema, metrics list, and rollout checklist. Wanted a quick gut-check first.

sara: this looks practical and incremental. Happy for RFC when you're ready.

alex: great — will ping when draft is up.
